survey: A western saddle hangs over a wooden fence rail. The rail runs left to right behind the saddle, with a vertical post on the far right of the full card. The saddle's long axis runs along the rail, horn at the left and cantle at the right. The horn neck rises from a stitched ring on the raised pommel and ends in a flat cap. The seat is a dished panel with a suede insert that curves up into the cantle. The near-side skirt hangs flat in front of the rail, and its bottom edge sits below the rail. The far skirt shows only as a thin edge past the right end of the rail, so the saddle straddles the rail the way a stored saddle would. The near stirrup leather comes out from under the seat rim, runs down over the skirt and ends in a metal buckle. Below the buckle, a short leather loop holds a wooden stirrup. The far stirrup's strap comes out from under the skirts, hanging lower and set back to the right. The depth offset matches a stirrup on the other side of the rail. Both stirrup treads are level and face the same way. There is no cinch or rigging, which is a normal simplification for a card.
